findings.trigger_condition: Input contains unhashable nodes (such as lists or dicts) or a mixture of unhashable and hashable nodes.
findings.root_cause: In _id_of(), looking up unhashable nodes performs an O(U + H) linear scan over unhashable_ids and hashable_ids. Additionally, looking up hashable nodes unconditionally performs a linear scan over unhashable_ids even when the node is hashable and already matched in hash_buckets. This degrades node registration to O(N) per edge when unhashable nodes are present.
findings.impact: O(N^2) time complexity during node registration and deduplication, causing severe performance degradation and potential execution timeouts on graphs containing unhashable nodes.
findings.suggested_validation: Benchmark dependency_layers with an edge stream containing 5,000 unhashable nodes (e.g. [([i], [i+1]) for i in range(5000)]); execution time scales quadratically instead of linearly.
